source_name: ERAR (KPK) — public-money transaction application
why_relevant: Successor to Supervizor, run by the Commission for the Prevention of Corruption (KPK) under Art. 75.a/75.b ZIntPK. Shows actual transactions from public bodies and state/municipality-owned companies to named suppliers, and since the 2025 relaunch also e-invoices of budget users from Sep 2024. This converts awarded contracts into realised spend — revealing what CIT firms, ATM vendors, terminal suppliers and core-banking integrators are actually paid, including under contracts never competitively tendered.

source_name: Državna revizijska komisija (DKOM) — decisions database and eRevizija
why_relevant: Independent review body ruling on the legality of procurement procedures. Its published decisions quote tender specifications, competitor objections, pricing structures and technical requirements in unusual detail — often the only public place where an ATM/POS/CIT specification and the competitive dynamics between bidders are laid out. Review filings are made via the eRevizija portal.

source_name: MJU Direktorat za javno naročanje — annual statistical reports on awarded public contracts
why_relevant: Statutory annual statistical report (Statistično poročilo o oddanih javnih naročilih) adopted by government, broken down by procedure, sector and subject; provides denominators for market sizing (e.g. total public procurement value EUR 9.17bn in 2023) and the official category taxonomy against which banking/security/IT lots can be positioned.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — razpisi / javna naročila (central bank as contracting authority)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and procures cash-cycle infrastructure: banknote processing and authentication machines, numismatic production, cash logistics, vault and security services, and IT. Its own notices (and its statement that all procurement documentation is published on enarocanje.si) map the state-side cash-handling supply chain. Its Katalog informacij javnega značaja is the formal transparency index.

source_name: Računsko sodišče RS — audit reports and audit archive
why_relevant: The Court of Audit routinely examines whether auditees ran lawful procurement and how they manage cash handling and banking/payment arrangements. Audit reports name suppliers, contract values, and irregularities (e.g. contracts concluded without a procurement procedure) — an independent quality check on the procurement record and a pointer to off-portal spend.

source_name: javnirazpisi.com — commercial Slovenian/European tender aggregator
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator indexing Slovenian and EU tenders with e-mail alerting and its own topical taxonomy. Useful as a discovery/pointer layer to find notice titles and contracting authorities that keyword search on the official portal misses, and to surface the local phrasing vendors actually use.

source_name: javni-razpisi.si (EUJN) — tender alerting service
why_relevant: Second Slovenian aggregator/alerting service covering national and EU notices; cross-checking two aggregators plus the official portal reduces the chance of missing an award notice with idiosyncratic wording (e.g. 'samopostrežne naprave' instead of 'bankomati').

source_name: SPOT / eVEM — licensing register for cash transport and valuables protection (prevoz in varovanje gotovine)
why_relevant: Defines the regulated activity and licence requirements for cash-in-transit in Slovenia (own or contracted monitoring centre, liability insurance, premises in Slovenia, at least one CIT vehicle). Establishes the universe of legally eligible CIT bidders — the set of companies that can win a Slovenian cash-transport tender — and the compliance criteria those tenders will cite.

source_name: PISRS — Pravilnik o načinu prevoza in varovanja gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih pošiljk
why_relevant: The binding rulebook setting methods, minimum conditions and security measures for transferring, transporting and protecting cash. Slovenian CIT and ATM-replenishment tenders reference these categories directly, so it supplies the controlled vocabulary (transport classes, vehicle/escort requirements) needed to parse tender specifications correctly.

source_name: ZPJS — Zakon o plačilnih in javnofinančnih storitvah (payment services for budget users / UJP)
why_relevant: Governs how payment and public-finance services are provided to direct and indirect state budget users and municipalities, and includes provisions on contracting authorities reporting executed payments under procurement contracts. Explains WHY certain bank/payment services for the public sector are routed via UJP rather than tendered on the open market — critical for correctly interpreting the absence of bank-service tenders on the portal.

source_name: NLB Group Investor Relations (nlbgroup.com) — financial reports, investor news, Investor Day decks
why_relevant: NLB is Slovenia's largest bank and the only listed one (LJSE + LSE GDRs), so it is under continuous disclosure obligation. IR hub carries annual reports, quarterly presentations and Investor Day decks that disclose branch counts, ATM fleet, card portfolio, digital/mobile user counts and fee income split (cards and ATM operations named explicitly in fee commentary). Best single window on private-bank network and card metrics in SI.

source_name: NLB financna porocila / letna porocila PDF archive (nlb.si investor section)
why_relevant: Slovenian-language annual report archive with stable, year-foldered PDF paths (e.g. .../2023/nlb-lp-2023-slo.pdf and English twin .../eng/.../nlb-ar-2023-eng.pdf). Contains the fullest narrative on poslovna mreza (branch network), stevilo bankomatov, karticno poslovanje and digital banking adoption — detail often trimmed from investor decks.

source_name: NLB Group interim (quarterly) reports and unaudited results packs
why_relevant: Quarterly cadence gives an intra-year signal on network rationalisation and card/ATM fee income, useful for detecting ATM fleet reduction or channel migration before the annual report confirms it.

source_name: OTP banka d.d. (ex Nova KBM + SKB) — Financna porocila in dokumenti
source_subtype: bank financial reports page + PDF archive
why_relevant: Second systemic bank after the 22 Aug 2024 Nova KBM/SKB merger; claims the largest branch and ATM network in Slovenia. Its annual report is the only disclosure of the merged network size, combined ATM fleet and card portfolio migration (SKB Visa vs NKBM Mastercard estates). Legacy Nova KBM and SKB reports are still hosted here via downloadfile.ashx ids, giving pre-merger baselines.

source_name: Letno porocilo 2024 OTP Skupine Slovenija in OTP banke d.d. (full PDF)
why_relevant: First post-merger annual report for the combined OTP Slovenia group; the single document containing the consolidated branch/ATM/card figures for the merged bank. Mirrored on a third-party site, which is itself useful as a fallback when the bank's own path rotates.

source_name: SKB banka letna porocila archive (skb.si) — pre-merger baseline
why_relevant: SKB's last standalone annual reports (through FY2023) hold the pre-merger branch count, ATM fleet and Visa card portfolio that the merged OTP entity absorbed. Essential for building a continuous series across the merger break; the domain may be retired, so archive early.

source_name: OTP banka — Zdruzena mreza bankomatov / Poslovalnice in bankomati locator
why_relevant: Public branch/ATM locator pages are an unintended near-real-time census of the physical estate: they reveal ATM and branch counts and locations between annual reports, and the 'merged ATM network' page states the shared-fleet arrangement (~450 ATMs across the two legacy estates, ~400 free-withdrawal ATMs). Best available proxy for fleet change tracking.

source_name: NLB bankomati locator (nlb.si/osebno/bankomati) and NLB kartice product pages
why_relevant: Same indirect-reveal logic for the market leader: the ATM locator enumerates the live fleet and the kartice pages enumerate the card product range (scheme mix, contactless, limits), which together let you track estate and portfolio changes between reports.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG — Financial Reports and Investor Relations (Slovenia segment)
source_subtype: listed parent IR / consolidated financial reports
why_relevant: Addiko is Vienna-listed and reports by country segment, so Slovenia gets its own segment disclosure (branch counts, digital/mobile penetration, consumer and SME lending, card-linked fee income) at group-report quality and quarterly cadence — far richer than the Slovenian subsidiary's own site.

source_name: Addiko Bank Slovenija (addiko.si) — card and payment product/tariff pages
why_relevant: The Slovenian subsidiary publishes no local annual report on its site (searches returned only product pages), so its card range, payment-services timetable (urnik placilnih storitev) and tariff documents are the only local-language disclosure of scheme mix, pricing and payment cut-offs. Useful for competitive card-pricing tracking rather than volumes.

source_name: Banka Intesa Sanpaolo d.d. (Slovenia) — Letno porocilo PDF series
why_relevant: Locally published, full Slovenian-language annual report with an explicit POSLOVNA MREZA (business network) section — branch counts, ATM and card commentary for a mid-tier player. Stable per-year URL pattern makes a long series easy to assemble (2018 through 2024 already visible).

source_name: Gorenjska banka d.d., Kranj — Letna porocila in razkritja dodatnih informacij
why_relevant: AIK-banka-owned mid-tier bank with a well-maintained annual report index going back to 2012 (uniform wp-content PDF paths). Reports carry network, card and payment-transaction commentary plus Pillar 3 'razkritja' — a rare long uninterrupted series for a private Slovenian bank.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica d.d. Ljubljana — letna porocila (dh.si/doc/letna-porocila)
why_relevant: The fastest-growing domestically owned savings bank and, unusually, a principal Mastercard licence holder that also issues cards on behalf of three other Slovenian institutions — so its report discloses cards-in-issue (~239k at end-2022), ATM replacement programmes and the DH Denarnik mobile wallet. Directly relevant to issuing-side and ATM-refresh demand signals.

source_name: Banka Sparkasse d.d. — Letna porocila in dodatna razkritja
why_relevant: Erste/Steiermarkische-owned mid-tier bank not named in the cell seed but squarely in scope as a private issuer; publishes local annual reports plus Pillar 3 'dodatna razkritja'. Also operates Sparkasse Pay d.o.o., a payments subsidiary that signals acquiring/payment-service activity.

source_name: Hranilnica LON d.d., Kranj — informacije za delnicarje in vlagatelje / letna porocila
why_relevant: Small savings bank with a shareholder-information page and a long PDF run of letna porocila; operates ~14 branches. Small players show technology-refresh decisions (card issuing outsourcing, ATM sharing) more explicitly than the systemic banks and are indicative of the tail of the SI issuing market.

source_name: Primorska hranilnica Vipava d.d. — Javne objave in porocila
why_relevant: Completes the private-issuer census for Slovenia; maintains a public reports page with annual reports back to at least 2015. Low individual value but necessary for a full-market denominator on branches, ATMs and cards outside the systemic banks.

source_name: Bizi.si / CompanyWall.si / eBonitete.si — Slovenian company registries with per-bank branch (poslovne enote) listings
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregators republish AJPES-derived data including each bank's registered poslovne enote (branch establishments) and filed financials. This is an independent cross-check on self-reported branch counts and a way to date branch closures during the OTP network consolidation.
